winner.title: Mukeke Recipe (Burundi)

evidence.authenticity: Burundian tourism site; fried-then-simmered tomato/onion/garlic fish, mentions grilling over coals, serves with ugali/uburobe/plantain. Author not named; only brief background (emblematic fish of Lake Tanganyika).
evidence.precision: Volumes only (1 cup peanut oil, 1/2 L water), no weights, no fish weight, no pot size, no frying time. Only doneness cue: flesh tender and has absorbed sauce; simmer 30-40 min.
evidence.testing: No sign of testing, no reasoning beyond 'do not turn or it breaks' and lemon rub to reduce smell.
evidence.photos: No photos seen in fetched content; no structured data.
evidence.efficiency: Short, no wasted steps; 30-40 min simmer plausible.
evidence.access: Fresh mukeke is unobtainable in the US and no substitute is named (tilapia would work).

winner.why: It is the only source I read that is clearly Burundian and actually the named dish, though it falls well under 60.

runnerUp.title: Whole Fresh Fried Tilapia

evidence.authenticity: Ugandan lake-fish preparation, not Burundian mukeke; useful only as a technique proxy for a whole fried lake fish. Uses Royco.
evidence.precision: Oil depth 2.5 cm, bread-cube oil test, 5-7 min per side until skin crisp; flour in cups, no fish weights.
evidence.testing: Some reasoning (do not turn early, skin breaks); no named author.
evidence.access: Whole tilapia and Royco (sub: bouillon) are easy in the US.

runnerUp.why: Better written but it is a different dish, so it cannot be the winner.

candidates.disqualified: Unattributed content-farm style page on a bare-IP domain; claims (palm oil, chili) contradict UN Tourism; no author
Ethiopian semek; no steps in schema, paywalled

searches: Burundian fried tilapia mukeke grilled fish recipe
notes: No test-kitchen or reputable cookbook source for mukeke exists in what I found. Only Burundi Travel gives a usable Burundian recipe; it is thin (no weights, no cues). The UN Tourism page (Kamwenubusa Jean Claude, mukeke pan-fried with garlic, traditionally with cow butter) is the authoritative description but returned 403 so it is not recorded as a recipe. A US cook would substitute whole tilapia or perch. Few distinct sites were available, so the 3-candidates-from-2-sites rule was met only by counting non-matching proxies; a retry with native-language (French) searches may help.
